QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_28

answer.text: Preventing the same income from being taxed in both countries

explanation.text: The Logic: Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements aim to avoid or eliminate double taxation of the same income in both the source country and the residence country, which can affect the tax outcome for offshore investors in an AIF. Their application is subject to the relevant DTAA terms, the Multilateral Instrument, and anti-avoidance rules such as GAAR, so professional tax advice is typically required. The Trap: Eliminating all taxes, guaranteeing returns, or providing SEBI registration exemptions overstate or misstate what a DTAA actually does — it allocates and avoids overlapping taxation, nothing more. Note: Based on NISM Series XIX-A workbook pages 260 and 261, which describe the purpose of DTAAs in avoiding double taxation, subject to DTAA/MLI/GAAR considerations.
